sample.title: Why Brazil Can’t Hide From Its Debt
sample.description:
As Brazil heads into an election, its debt problems are becoming harder to ignore. Consumers and businesses are struggling with sky-high borrowing costs as the country’s deteriorating fiscal outlook alarms investors. 

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has rolled out measures aimed at easing the pressure on families and businesses while his main rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, has promised tighter spending controls, albeit with few details. Whoever wins the presidency is likely to face difficult choices over how to bring the country’s debt to heel.

sample.title: Inside Texas's Growing Political Fight Over Data Centers
sample.description:
Texas has long attracted data centers with its pro-business policies and abundance of land. Today, it’s one of the biggest data center hubs in the country, but residents are starting to push back over issues like transparency, water use and power bills. CNBC traveled to Texas to learn how the growing backlash has made data centers a key issue in the upcoming race between Ken Paxton and James Talarico–and in midterm elections across the country.

sample.title: Thousands of illegal 'ghost plates' on cars revealed by new cameras | BBC News
sample.description:
Thousands of illegal registration plates on cars and other vehicles have been detected by a new camera system currently being tested on motorways in south-east England, BBC Panorama has revealed.

These 'ghost plates' have been adapted to avoid their details being identified by automatic number plate recognition systems, which are used to enforce speed limits and low emission zones as well as to track criminals.

Illegal plates are putting the public at risk and are far too easy to get hold of, according to one former government advisor.

sample.title: Police block Drumcree Orange Order parade in Portadown, Northern Ireland, after protests | BBC News
sample.description:
Police have stopped a controversial Orange Order parade, after protests in Portadown.
 
The Drumcree parade, which in the 1990s sparked some of the most serious disorder in Northern Ireland's history, was due to go ahead for the first time in 30 years after a series of legal challenges.
 
But the Orange Order was unable to make the permitted parade on Sunday morning as protesters gathered in the area. The stand-off continued throughout Sunday, and early-morning attempts on Monday to re-start the parade were blocked by police.

5 terror arrests at airbase used by US bombers - possible Iran link investigated | BBC News
sample.description:
Five men have been arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act and explosive offences after three suspicious vehicles were reported near RAF Fairford airbase in Gloucestershire, England.

A major incident was declared and dozens of homes near the facility were evacuated.  The base is used by US bombers carrying out airstrikes against Iran. 

An Army explosive ordnance disposal team examined vehicles near the base, with counter-terror police leading the investigation.

President Donald Trump said those arrested had been "looking to do big damage", adding: "We had them under view for a long time, and we got them."  

The US Department of Defense raised the threat level at RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk - which hosts the USAF's 48th Fighter Wing - to its second-highest category.

UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he had been in contact with his US counterpart, Pete Hegseth.
